picks.headline: Canadian author Thélyson Orélien accused of using AI to write award-winning novel
picks.excerpt: Canadian-Haitian author Thélyson Orélien is accused of using AI to write most of his award-winning debut novel C’était ça ou mourir; his Canadian and French publishers are standing by him.
picks.rationale: Freshest hard-news item (09-23): a prize-winning debut novel accused of being mostly AI-written, and both of its publishers are standing by the author. It raises the authorship question with a named book, a named prize and two publishers on record.
picks.framing_note: WRITER: attribute the accusation to its source. The publishers stand by him, so do not present the AI use as established fact. Keep it distinct from earlier AI-allegation cards (Daggermouth 07-30/08-06, Commonwealth prize 06-27): this case is a new author, a new book and a French-language market.

picks.headline: Novvel.co pioneers producing graphic novels with AI assistance
picks.excerpt: Singapore startup Novvel.co says its AI-assisted platform can halve graphic-novel adaptation production time and cost, with human artists still in the driver's seat.
picks.rationale: The most actionable pick for visual creators: a production workflow that claims to halve the time and cost of graphic-novel adaptation while keeping human artists involved. It shows how AI is entering comics and illustration pipelines.
picks.framing_note: WRITER: lead with how the workflow splits work between AI and human artists. The 'halves time/cost' figure is the company's own claim, so attribute it. Keep funding or valuation details out.

picks.headline: 웹소설 플랫폼, AI로 찍어낸 '쌀먹' 웹소설 대량 유입에 골머리
picks.excerpt: 리디 등 웹소설 플랫폼에 AI로 복붙 생산한 웹소설이 대량 유입되며 'AI 쌀먹' 문제로 플랫폼이 골머리를 앓고 있다.
picks.rationale: A Korean-market angle the section hasn't covered: web-novel platforms such as Ridi are dealing with a flood of AI-produced serials written to farm platform rewards. It is the local counterpart to the Amazon AI-slop stories covered earlier, but a different market and a different event.
picks.framing_note: WRITER: explain 'AI 쌀먹' (mass-producing low-effort AI serials to farm rewards or revenue), then say what the platforms are doing about it. Do not re-cite the Amazon AI-slop study (covered 08-29).

picks.headline: ScrollEd wants to turn textbooks into TikTok
picks.excerpt: ScrollEd uses AI to turn textbooks into a scrollable, short-form feed of video, audio and quizzes.
picks.rationale: A new product that changes the reading format: AI turns textbook content into a short-form feed of video, audio and quizzes. It is a concrete format and UX change, and it adds the education angle to the day's spread.
picks.framing_note: WRITER: focus on the format change (book to feed) and how the product works. Leave out funding figures if the article includes them.

picks.headline: Misconduct case dropped against AI ethicist Virginia Dignum after claims of AI use in her book
picks.excerpt: Sweden's research-misconduct board dismissed a case against AI ethicist Virginia Dignum after allegations her book The AI Paradox contained AI-hallucinated references.
picks.rationale: A regulator ruling rather than an opinion: Sweden's misconduct board dismissed allegations that hallucinated references in an AI ethicist's own book were AI-generated. It is a nonfiction and citation-integrity case, a different angle from rank 1's fiction authorship dispute, and it comes with a book-specific image.
picks.framing_note: WRITER: report what the board decided and why. Keep it distinct from rank 1: this is about nonfiction citations and a formal misconduct ruling, not a novel.
